newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Moslem group apologises for Java church attack.
newsitem.headline: Moslem group apologises for Java church attack.

text.p: The leader of Indonesia's largest Moslem group has publicly apologised and asked for forgiveness for an attack by thousands of Moslems on churches in East Java last week in which five people died, a statement on Monday said.

Abdurrahman Wahid, leader of the 30-million-strong Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), said in the statement sent to Reuters that the rioting in the town of Situbondo in East Java province on Thursday was most likely carried out by NU members as the province is the group's heartland.

The Jakarta Post newspaper on Monday said 21 Christian churches, five Catholic elementary schools, and one Christian orphanage, among other buildings, were burned in Situbondo after attacks by an angry mob of around 10,000 people.

Police in the town had earlier said nine churches, four schools, a convent and a court house were burned. State Secretary Murdiono said on Friday around 2,000 to 3,000 people had rioted but that security had been quickly restored.

"Those who carried out the 'Situbondo Incident' were generally NU members and this incident becomes the moral responsibilty of the national NU leadership, including myself as chairman," Wahid, a high-profile intellectual, said.
"I, as head, apologise for the losses which are suffered by the government and community and express my deep condolences to the victims who died and were injured," Wahid said.
"I ask for God to forgive those who did this thing without knowing the serious consequences for the community, nation and state," he said.
Wahid said it was ironic that he heard of the incident while returning from Rome, where he had participated in an international meeting on peace that was attended by both Moslem and Christian groups.
The riot broke out after a court hearing into a case of alleged blasphemy against Islam in Situbondo, about 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second city, Surabaya.

Several thousand people outside the court during the third hearing of the case called for the accused, a Moslem identified as Mohamad Saleh, to be sentenced immediately or to be handed over to the crowd.
The official Antara news agency said local security agents were questioning 40 suspects. Officials said on Friday that at least 120 people had been initially detained.
The incident was the latest in a series of attacks on Christian establishments, blamed by religious scholars on economic pressure and religious rivalries.
A hall used by Catholics for worship in an East Jakarta village was burned down last month. A number of churches were burned in the Surabaya area in June.
